blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: hash — Fixed-size digest of arbitrary input.
collision — Two inputs producing the same digest.
salt — Random value mixed into password hashing.
integrity — Confidence that data has not changed.

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.text: A cryptographic hash transforms an arbitrary input into a fixed-size digest. It is designed to make reversing the digest infeasible, not impossible under all circumstances.

blocks.title: Trace
blocks.text: A message digest supports integrity checking when the reference hash is trusted. Hash collisions can exist because outputs have finite length.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Passwords should be processed using a salted, purpose-built slow password-hashing scheme, not simply a fast general-purpose hash and never reversible encryption.
